claim: 28.5% of a 49-task sample of SWE-bench Verified have test suites weak enough that a Docker-verified incorrect patch passes them.
stance_target: whole-task test suites in code RL/eval environments are frequently hackable
quoted_support: On a 49-task sample of SWE-bench Verified, 28.5% of tasks have test suites weak enough that a Docker-verified incorrect patch passes them.

claim: On R2E-Gym tasks across 6 repositories, single-shot exploit generation against the test harness succeeds 25.0% of the time.
stance_target: code RL environments are exploitable via weak verifiers
quoted_support: On 20 R2E-Gym tasks across 6 repositories, the same pipeline at single-shot exploit generation yields 25.0%.

claim: Within the same human-rated difficulty stratum, frontier model Pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified is 14.14 percentage points higher on tasks flagged as hackable than on robust tasks, across a meta-analysis of 134 model submissions.
stance_target: test-suite weakness inflates measured model performance (reward hacking proxy at task level)
scope_conditions: SWE-bench Verified leaderboard, 134 frontier model submissions
quoted_support: A random-effects meta-analysis over 134 frontier model submissions to SWE-bench Verified finds, within the same human-rated difficulty stratum, model Pass@1 is +14.14 percentage points higher on flagged-hackable tasks than on robust ones (95% CI [+11.80, +16.48]; one-sided p < 10^-6; I^2 = 0%; 123 of 134 models positive).

claim: An inline LLM judge gated by a Docker gold-sanity check (running each generated test against the gold solution before consulting the judge) flags 65 of 105 decisive LLM-generated tests as failing on the gold patch itself, a defect rate the LLM judge alone misses.
stance_target: LLM judges alone are unreliable for detecting weak/hackable test augmentations; gold-sanity gating is necessary
scope_conditions: 11 broken SWE-bench Verified tasks, hardening procedure
quoted_support: the gate flags 65 of 105 decisive LLM-generated tests as failing on the gold patch itself, a 61.9% per-augmentation defect rate the LLM judge alone misses.

claim: This audit operates at whole-task granularity (does any incorrect patch pass the FULL test suite) rather than localizing hackability to individual unit-test methods/sub-requirements within a task.
stance_target: granularity gap that a per-requirement harness could fill
quoted_support: On a 49-task sample of SWE-bench Verified, 28.5% of tasks have test suites weak enough that a Docker-verified incorrect patch passes them.
